# Feature decisions and engine findings

These are findings from the 1.01.07 Windows build, not guarantees for future patches. Read the current implementation before reusing a path or constant.

## Runtime and settings

- `Scripts/main.lua` passes a shared mod table to modules. Use its `valid`, `lib`, `widget`, `warn`, `hook`, and `reset` helpers. The hook helper coalesces callbacks per path and retries binding when classes load. Blueprint post callbacks use argument 2 of `RegisterHook`; native `/Script/` post callbacks use argument 3. Run Unreal calls on the game thread; prefer `LoopInGameThreadWithDelay`, not `LoopAsync`.
- World travel can free actors. Keep paths rather than long-lived actor references and resolve on use; clear world-specific state on reset. Don't use `FindAllOf` on every tick. Discover pickups at BeginPlay, cap and spread active work, and handle pickups collected, hidden, or out of range. Temporary marker meshes must not collide, cast shadows, or generate overlaps.
- `features.ini` is shared by both native selectors: `shimmer=0..4` means Off, Low, Mid (default `2`), High, Over Here!; `enemyHpBars=0..2` means Off, HP bar, HP bar + damage (default `2`). **Do not reintroduce `shimmer.txt` or `damageNumbers`.** Lua treats `0` as true: test numeric modes explicitly. `options.lua` updates a single digit while preserving comments and line endings. Shimmer applies live; other settings preview immediately but apply in gameplay after restart. Travel Stride ships off.

## Video menu and item data

- The native Video page is `Video_OptionsList_C` inside `OptionsMenu_C`. Its preview is a streamed scene with a rotating `VideoConfigVisualizer_C`, not a static background. Wait for `page.ConfigVisInst` and floor collision; the title screen works without a gameplay character. Native controls use `SkipSavingOption`; don't write mod preferences into the game's SystemSave.
- Keep one non-interactive **BBM Settings** heading, not a prefix on every row. Keep the inline heading visible on hover and focus. Pin the title only when the heading scrolls out of view. The native `VideoHeader` is a named child of the `VideoOptions` canvas, not necessarily an exposed property. A stationary mouse must not trap focus when using a controller.
- Visual rows come first: graphics, pickup shimmer, enemy HP bars, item description stats, status effect names. The other rows explain their effects in text. A fake healing-stat square is not an inventory preview. The right panel is hit-test invisible; entering or leaving it must not disrupt input, the real camera, or saves.
- Graphics compares render resolutions from the **same fixed shot**. Shimmer shows a non-collectible herb at the seated skeleton's feet: native herb mesh with `HealingHerbs_02_MI`, corresponding to Royal Dried Herbs. Trace the floor at visualizer-relative X `+123`, Y `-151`; offset by the scaled mesh's local lower Z. Do not attach the item to the orbit or spawn an interactable/savable pickup.
- Item cards rotate every **3 s**: Royal Dried Herbs, Holy Sword Endu (`FlyingSword` internally), Chakram, Iron Pineapple, Roasted Ojum Lizard. Share `buildItemStatRows`; pass `baseValuesOnly` so the preview doesn't need a combat pawn. Toggling stats changes only their visibility.
- Font names alone can give a false match. Native titles and stats use `CommonTextBlock:SetStyle` with `BigTextStyle` and `StatText`. Use `FS_DescriptionText` for lore: it selects `DescriptionRichText` or `DescriptionRichText_Light` from `CommonUI.FontStyleOverride`. Set the localized lore directly on `MainTextBlock`; don't invoke the inventory item-binding event from the Video menu. Check regular and light glyphs against a live inspect widget at the same screen position, not just the font fields on its template.
- For live items, read both native weapon attack getters and the player's balance scale. `IncreaseFromLevel` is already a fraction; do **not** divide it by base attack. Match native float multiplication before flooring attack values. Preserve flat vs percent units, charge/return time, signed item bonuses, and unsigned status-screen healing percentages.
- Status previews show the **moving** native orbit. Attach a dedicated scene capture to `visualizer.Camera`; redraw while this row is active. Cycle **Poison, Weaken, Burn** every **2 s** with the game's own UI materials and private dynamic instances (`Scale`, `Opacity`, `Pulse`). Some materials draw nothing until their parameters are set. Toggle only the lower-left name; don't stop motion or the effects. There is **no floating herb icon** in this preview. The actual gameplay names do belong above the usable-item icon. Destroy captures, release render targets, and drop widget references on exit/reset.

## Rendering, widescreen and pickup markers

- Native resolution needs the game's `UpdateScreen%` path to update render targets, not just `r.ScreenPercentage`. Scope overrides of `LockedResScale` and `ResScale` to the native call and restore the saved options. The preset also sets TAA, 16x anisotropy, and the pixel-filter/dither material collection. `screenPercentage` in `features.ini` defaults to 100%; 125/150% supersampling costs GPU time.
- Distinguish geometry edges from texture detail. Sampled cooked textures: coin and one interior floor 128x128, herb and library/catacomb bricks 256x256, a castle floor and bark 512x512. Several textures explicitly specify `TF_Nearest`; the World texture group also uses point filtering. An anisotropy cap does not override every sampler. Testing smoother world sampling is a possible experiment, **not a shipped fix**. Compare a wall head-on and a floor at a shallow angle; leave UI textures alone.
- Ultrawide must fix both `FirstPersonCamera.bConstrainAspectRatio` and native HUD positions. Move the status cluster and usable item left, compass right, accounting for viewport DPI. Names follow the item's own canvas. Poison and other screen borders need edge coverage without changing their 16:9 appearance. A previous 1680x720 test exposed 200 blank pixels on each side. Recheck after resize and when returning to 16:9.
- High shimmer uses `GodRay_Cutout` with `M_GodRay_Animated`: 140 cm tall, 16 cm wide, brightness 5, vertical rotation and the game's custom primitive data. `LoadAsset` needs the **full object path including `.ObjectName`**; a component can exist but render nothing. Over Here! is a red cylinder and inverted cone using the emissive mesh material. Restore the pickup's original material values and hide old markers on Off, mode changes, collection, or leaving range. Re-enabling must reuse parts, not stack arrows.

## Gameplay boundaries

- **Health:** Off hides the entire native enemy **and boss** bar even after retargeting. Bar-only shows current/max HP without hit tracking. Bar + damage flashes the last hit at the right end of the **actual name row**, not inside the fill or on an extra line. Test a long name, repeated equal hits, a target change, and expiry. Player HP is independent of the enemy mode.
- **Drag:** Native inventory rules still decide compatible weapon/throwable/charm slots. Don't replace normal click-to-equip.
- **Travel Stride:** Configurable out-of-combat delay (12 s by default) on any ground, +25% ground speed, double flying-sword dash recharge. No explored-route tracking. Aggro or combat damage resets the timer. A jump or ledge removes only extra horizontal speed, including the cached takeoff speed; preserve vertical motion and resume speed on landing. Banking charge before a fight is intentional. Earlier in-game comparison: 400 vs 500 cm/s, recharge progress 0.1 vs 0.2, no longer jump.
- **F5/F9:** Pin progression, not a fight in motion. F5 requires a monument save, writes player status into the active object, serializes a **private clone**, and adds the game's validated safe location, level streaming and music data. Validate the new file before rotation; keep one `.prev`. F9 validates slot/version/map, sets **both** active save references and opens the level; confirm through `RestoreSuspend`. Don't overwrite monument or native recovery files, select the newest native save, or promise exact airborne coordinates/AI/projectile/lift state. Keep refusal paths for death, menus, transitions, save blocks and incompatible maps.
- Native suspend was observed on a roughly 120 s timer subject to restrictions. Alt+F4 did not reliably write current progress. A useful regression case: pin 43 HP, 2 herbs and a world flag; create newer native progress at 28 HP and 7 herbs; reload the pin and compare native-file hashes before/after. Always use a disposable profile.
- F5 uses one private `.new` file: first serialize and reload progression to detach it, then overwrite it with the completed snapshot. Reopen it and check HP, position, and every entry in both safe-region lists **before** moving either existing generation. F9 never selects `.new` and falls back to `.prev` only when the primary is missing, not when it fails validation.
